newsitem.title: USA: Boeing cites sales volume for Q3 gains.
newsitem.headline: Boeing cites sales volume for Q3 gains.

text.p: Boeing Co on Thursday reported third quarter earnings rose to $0.74 per share from $0.66 a year earlier saying the gains were principally due to increased sales volume and higher interest income.

The compay said these factors were partially offset by higher research and development expense principally associated with the 737 derivatives -- the 737-600, 700, 800 aircraft -- and a higher effective income tax rate.
Sales for the three months ended September 30 were $5.60 billion, up from $4.38 billion in 1995's third quarter.

Boeing said airline announced order activity continues to be encouraging, with 435 airplanes ordered in the first nine months of 1996, reflecting continued increased growth in passenger traffic, load factors, and profitability by the airline industry as a whole.
The company noted it recently announced production rate increases on the 737 and 777 programs.

Boeing noted it will issue some $860 million of its common stock, assume $2.165 billion of Rockwell International Corp's debt and assume certain retiree obligations of Rockwell under an agreement to acquire its aerospace business.

The transaction is likely to be completed by the end of the year, Boeing said, adding it is expected to strengthen the strategic position of the Boeing defense and space segment, particularly with respect to space systems and information/battle management systems.
The $1 billion Boeing ShareValue Trust established July 1 allows employees to share in the results of their efforts to increase shareholder value over the long term, it noted.
The company said its third quarter net included a $4 million accrual for potentially distributable appreciation from the trust.

The trust will hold Boeing stock, and increases in the trust value due to dividends and higher stock prices above an annual three percent threshold will be periodically distributed to employees in the form of Boeing stock.

As of September 30, the increased value of the $500 million fund for Period 1 exceeded the threshold value by $4 million, although potential distributions would not occur until June 30, 1998, the company pointed out.
Based on current programs and schedules, research and development expense for the full year 1996 is projected to be in the $1.2 billion range, compared with $1.3 billion in 1995.
Corporate investment income was $58 million higher in the first nine months of 1996 than in the same period in 1995 due primarily to higher cash and short-term investment balances.

The effective income tax rate of 18.0 percent for the first nine months of 1996 reflects the recognition of a one-time tax benefit of $95 million related to prior years' investment tax credits, Boeing said.

Without the investment tax credit benefit, the effective income tax rate would have been 27.2 percent, 1.6 percent lower than previously estimated for the full year of 1996 due to the reinstatement of the research and experimentation tax credit effective July 1, 1996, and an increased foreign sales corporation tax benefit.

The 8.4 percent income tax rate for 1995 was the result of the $600 million pretax charge to earnings for the special retirement program and the recognition of significant research and experimentation tax credits in 1995.
